text: The report of my death was an exaggeration. Those are Mark Twain's real words, printed in eighteen ninety seven.
So why does everyone quote them wrong? That spring, papers said he was dying of a broken heart in London.
He wasn't. His cousin had been sick. Twain told a reporter: I have even heard on good authority that I was dead.
Ten years later, papers said he was lost at sea on a yacht. He was at home in New York.
And that day, a Washington paper repeated his celebrated statement as: the reports of my death have been greatly exaggerated.
Greatly was never in it. The papers edited the line you know. His was simpler. The report of my death was an exaggeration.
